# Ferrotensor

> Ferrotensor (also written Ferro Tensor) is a pure-Rust GPU machine-learning framework: tensors, reverse-mode autograd, `nn` layers, optimizers and LoRA fine-tuning that run on Metal, Vulkan or DX12 through wgpu and hand-written WGSL compute kernels, plus a CPU device used as the reference in tests. No CUDA, cuDNN or libtorch is needed. Python bindings wrap the same tensor API. Version {{ft_version}}, pre-1.0, f32 arithmetic and trainable parameters (frozen LoRA base weights are stored as f16 by default in the CLI), single GPU, licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0.

Install:

- Python 3.10+ (wheels for macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64): `pip install ferrotensor`
- Rust 1.88+ library: `cargo add ferrotensor`
- LoRA command-line tool (`train`, `eval`, `generate`): `cargo install ferrotensor-cli`

Tested on an NVIDIA A10G (24 GB) through Vulkan, an Apple M2 (8 GB) through Metal, and software Vulkan (Mesa lavapipe) in CI; other GPUs are untested. On the A10G, LoRA on SmolLM2-1.7B took held-out loss from 2.65 to 1.06 in 250 steps; against PyTorch + PEFT on CUDA with the same recipe on the same GPU, the held-out loss is identical before training and within 0.005 after, and Ferrotensor runs at 0.32 to 0.84 of PyTorch's speed. LoRA loss and gradients are checked against PyTorch autograd in CI. Peak GPU memory for LoRA on SmolLM2-1.7B is 8,222 MiB in 0.7 (11,607 MiB in 0.6) and 5,245 MiB with --checkpoint-blocks, with identical losses.

## Docs

- [Introduction](https://ferrotensor.dev/docs/): what Ferrotensor is and where to start
- [Installation](https://ferrotensor.dev/docs/installation.html): crate, CLI and Python package
- [Python quickstart](https://ferrotensor.dev/docs/python.html): train a model from Python, CPU or GPU
- [Use cases](https://ferrotensor.dev/docs/use-cases.html): runnable Rust examples with their real output
- [How-to guide](https://ferrotensor.dev/guide/): 19 step-by-step guides with real output, from installing and checking your GPU to LoRA fine-tuning, training in Rust or Python, and troubleshooting
- [LoRA fine-tuning walkthrough](https://ferrotensor.dev/docs/examples/lora-sft.html): end-to-end walkthrough with every command
- [Architecture](https://ferrotensor.dev/docs/architecture.html): how a tensor op reaches a WGSL kernel
- [Writing a kernel](https://ferrotensor.dev/docs/writing-a-kernel.html): adding a GPU op
- [Benchmarks](https://ferrotensor.dev/docs/benchmarks.html): kernel and tensor-API timings with method
- [About](https://ferrotensor.dev/about/): who builds Ferrotensor, what is measured, and how to get in touch
